statement: Long-acting reversible contraception (IUDs and implants) is 20x more effective than the pill/patch/ring in typical real-world use, because effectiveness does not depend on user action.
effect_size: Pill/patch/ring users had ~20x the contraceptive failure rate of LARC users (hazard ratio 21.8) in a prospective cohort
population: 9256 women, Contraceptive CHOICE Project, St. Louis

provenance.primary: Winner B et al., 'Effectiveness of long-acting reversible contraception', NEJM 2012;366:1998-2007
provenance.surfaced_via: Wave-42 reproductive brief; PubMed PMID 22621627 verified

confidence_notes: Large prospective cohort with free method provision (removes cost confounder). The typical-use vs perfect-use gap is the core mechanism: LARC removes the human from the loop. IUDs do NOT cause infertility (separate refuted myth).

statement: Contraceptive failure rates differ greatly between perfect use and typical use; combined pills fail ~7% and condoms ~13% in typical first-year use versus <1% for IUDs and implants.
effect_size: 1st-yr typical-use failure: implant ~0.05%, hormonal IUD ~0.2%, copper IUD ~0.8%, pill ~7%, male condom ~13%, withdrawal ~20%

provenance.primary: Trussell J, 'Contraceptive failure in the United States', Contraception 2011;83:397-404
provenance.surfaced_via: Wave-42 reproductive brief; PubMed PMID 21477680 verified

confidence_notes: The canonical US contraceptive-failure dataset. Typical use is the honest comparison unit. Condoms are mediocre contraception but the only method that also prevents STIs (dual-protection is their real value).

statement: HPV vaccination reduces the risk of invasive cervical cancer at the population level, with the largest effect when given before age 17 (~88% reduction).
effect_size: Vaccinated before age 17: IRR 0.12 (~88% reduction) for invasive cervical cancer; before age 30 overall ~63% reduction
population: ~1.67 million Swedish girls/women aged 10-30, national registry, 2006-2017

provenance.primary: Lei J et al., 'HPV Vaccination and the Risk of Invasive Cervical Cancer', NEJM 2020;383:1340-1348
provenance.surfaced_via: Wave-42 reproductive brief; PubMed PMID 32997908 verified

confidence_notes: First demonstration that an HPV vaccine prevents an INVASIVE cancer (prior trials showed precancer endpoints). Registry-grade. Underpins WHO cervical-cancer elimination strategy. Cross-ref oncogenic-virus story in section 26.

statement: Erectile dysfunction is an early marker of cardiovascular disease; new-onset ED in younger men predicts roughly 50% higher future cardiovascular event risk because penile arteries are small and clog first.
effect_size: ED associated with ~hazard ratio 1.25-1.5 for incident CV events; effect strongest in men <60
population: Olmsted County men cohort (Inman) + multiple meta-analyses

provenance.primary: Inman BA et al., 'A population-based, longitudinal study of erectile dysfunction and future coronary artery disease', Mayo Clin Proc 2009;84:108-113
provenance.surfaced_via: Wave-42 reproductive brief; cross-ref section 11 vascular

confidence_notes: Predictor-not-just-symptom: ED is a cardiovascular work-up trigger in younger men. PDE5 inhibitors treat the symptom; the vascular/metabolic disease (diabetes, hypertension, smoking) is the real target. Cross-ref section 11, 22.

statement: In middle-aged/older men with genuine hypogonadism and cardiovascular risk, testosterone-replacement therapy was non-inferior to placebo for major adverse cardiovascular events; it did not demonstrate benefit for optimizing healthy men.
effect_size: MACE 7.0% (TRT) vs 7.3% (placebo), met non-inferiority; higher rates of AFib, AKI, pulmonary embolism in TRT arm
population: 5246 men aged 45-80 with hypogonadism + CV risk, randomized placebo-controlled

provenance.primary: Lincoff AM et al. (TRAVERSE), 'Cardiovascular Safety of Testosterone-Replacement Therapy', NEJM 2023;389:107-117
provenance.surfaced_via: Wave-42 reproductive brief; PubMed PMID 37326322 verified

confidence_notes: Reassured on CV safety in DIAGNOSED hypogonadism; did NOT validate 'low-T' clinic optimization of the worried-well. TRT suppresses endogenous production and fertility. Cross-ref section 13 testosterone-clinic debunk.

statement: PSA-based prostate cancer screening reduces prostate-cancer mortality modestly but at the cost of substantial over-diagnosis and over-treatment, making it a shared individual decision rather than a blanket recommendation.
effect_size: ~21% relative reduction in prostate-cancer mortality; ~1 death prevented per ~1000 men screened over 11 years; ~27 extra cancers diagnosed per death prevented
population: 162,000+ men, European Randomized Study of Screening for Prostate Cancer (ERSPC)

provenance.primary: Schröder FH et al. (ERSPC), 'Prostate-cancer mortality at 11 years of follow-up', NEJM 2012;366:981-990
provenance.surfaced_via: Wave-42 reproductive brief; PubMed PMID 22417251 verified

confidence_notes: The over-diagnosis problem drives the shift to active surveillance for low-risk disease. Harms of treatment = incontinence and erectile dysfunction. Cross-ref section 25 oncology, 07 prevention.

statement: IVF live-birth rate per cycle using a woman's own eggs declines steeply with maternal age, from ~40-50% under 35 to under 5% over 42, driven by egg chromosomal quality.
population: US national ART surveillance (CDC/SART registry data)

provenance.primary: CDC/SART National ART Surveillance System annual reports; ASRM committee opinions on age and fertility
provenance.surfaced_via: Wave-42 reproductive brief; extends section 19 fertility

confidence_notes: No clinic protocol overrides egg age. Clinics quote favorable denominators (per-transfer/cumulative/subgroup) vs per-cycle-started. Donor eggs track the donor's young age (~50%+). Honest fertility-industry framing.

statement: Most IVF 'add-ons' (endometrial scratch, assisted hatching, time-lapse imaging, immune therapies, many supplements) lack good RCT evidence for improving live-birth rates yet are routinely sold at extra cost.
effect_size: UK HFEA rates most add-ons amber or red (insufficient or no evidence of live-birth benefit)
population: HFEA evidence-rating reviews; multiple Cochrane reviews

provenance.primary: HFEA Treatment Add-ons ratings (UK Human Fertilisation and Embryology Authority); Cochrane reviews of IVF adjuncts

confidence_notes: Clearest example of an evidence-light market sold to desperate patients. The regulator (HFEA) explicitly flags the lack of evidence.

statement: Elective egg freezing is a probability not a guarantee; per-oocyte live-birth chance is only ~6-7%, so meaningful odds require banking many eggs, and freezing before ~35 materially beats freezing later.
effect_size: Cumulative live-birth probability rises with oocyte number and falls with age at freezing; per-mature-oocyte ~6.5% in younger women
population: Large vitrified-oocyte cohorts (Cobo et al., Spain)

provenance.primary: Cobo A et al., 'Oocyte vitrification as an efficient option for elective fertility preservation', Fertil Steril 2016;105:755-764

confidence_notes: Vitrification is real technological progress but is marketed as insurance it cannot fully be. Sperm freezing, by contrast, is cheap and reliable. Ovarian tissue cryopreservation is now non-experimental.

statement: Endometriosis affects ~10% of reproductive-age women but has a mean diagnostic delay of roughly 7 years because pelvic pain is normalized and definitive diagnosis historically required laparoscopy.
effect_size: Mean diagnostic delay ~6.7 years across 10 countries; prevalence ~10% of reproductive-age women

provenance.primary: Nnoaham KE et al., 'Impact of endometriosis on quality of life and work productivity: a multicenter study across ten countries', Fertil Steril 2011;96:366-373
provenance.surfaced_via: Wave-42 reproductive brief; flagship under-diagnosed pain condition

confidence_notes: Pain severity does not track lesion size. Treatment is symptom-led, not curative. The clearest case where believing women's pain is itself the intervention.

statement: Polycystic ovary syndrome is the most common endocrine disorder of reproductive-age women (~6-13%) and is a metabolic disorder (insulin resistance, raised cardiometabolic/diabetes risk) as much as a reproductive one.
effect_size: Prevalence ~6% (NIH criteria) up to ~10-13% (Rotterdam criteria) by meta-analysis
population: Systematic review/meta-analysis of community-based prevalence studies

provenance.primary: Bozdag G et al., 'The prevalence and phenotypic features of polycystic ovary syndrome: a systematic review and meta-analysis', Hum Reprod 2016;31:2841-2855
provenance.surfaced_via: Wave-42 reproductive brief; cross-ref section 13 androgen axis, Domain D

confidence_notes: First-line levers are weight/insulin/lifestyle. Letrozole beats clomiphene for ovulation induction (Legro 2014, NEJM). Cross-ref insulin resistance Domain D.

statement: Letrozole is superior to clomiphene for ovulation induction and live birth in women with PCOS, making it first-line.
effect_size: Live birth 27.5% (letrozole) vs 19.1% (clomiphene); higher ovulation and cumulative live-birth rates
population: 750 women with PCOS, randomized double-blind trial

provenance.primary: Legro RS et al., 'Letrozole versus Clomiphene for Infertility in the Polycystic Ovary Syndrome', NEJM 2014;371:119-129

confidence_notes: RCT-grade. Changed first-line practice for PCOS ovulation induction.

statement: Low-dose aspirin started in early pregnancy substantially reduces preterm preeclampsia in high-risk women.

provenance.primary: Rolnik DL et al. (ASPRE), 'Aspirin versus Placebo in Pregnancies at High Risk for Preterm Preeclampsia', NEJM 2017;377:613-622
provenance.surfaced_via: Wave-42 reproductive brief; cross-ref section 19 pregnancy

confidence_notes: One of the highest-value prenatal interventions; RCT-grade. Preeclampsia is a leading cause of maternal death. Cross-ref section 19.

statement: The vagina is a self-cleaning organ; 'vaginal detox' products, jade eggs, yoni pearls, and douching have no benefit and are associated with harm (douching linked to bacterial vaginosis, PID, and ectopic pregnancy).
effect_size: Douching associated with increased BV, PID, and ectopic pregnancy risk; jade-egg claims unsupported (GOOP settled a regulatory lawsuit)
population: Multiple observational studies on vaginal douching; regulatory action on jade eggs

provenance.primary: Cottrell BH, 'An updated review of evidence to discourage douching', MCN Am J Matern Child Nurs 2010; CA regulatory settlement re: GOOP jade-egg claims 2018

confidence_notes: The 'cleaning' product causes the problems it claims to prevent. A self-cleaning organ does not need a product. Vaginal steaming can cause burns.

statement: Beyond correcting deficiency and preconception folate (which prevents neural-tube defects), most marketed 'fertility-boosting' supplements have weak-to-absent live-birth evidence.
effect_size: Cochrane review of antioxidants for male subfertility: evidence for live birth low-quality and inconclusive
population: Cochrane systematic reviews (antioxidants, male and female subfertility)

provenance.primary: de Ligny W et al., 'Antioxidants for male subfertility', Cochrane Database Syst Rev 2022

confidence_notes: Folate genuinely prevents NTDs. Myo-inositol (PCOS), CoQ10, vitamin D (if deficient) are least-bad candidates with preliminary support, not guarantees. Most 'fertility blends' are hope sold by the bottle.

statement: Drugs marketed for female low sexual desire (flibanserin, bremelanotide) have small average effects, meaningful side-effects, and are not a 'female Viagra'.
effect_size: Flibanserin: ~0.5 additional satisfying sexual events/month over placebo, with dizziness/somnolence/hypotension; modest benefit-risk

provenance.primary: Jaspers L et al., 'Efficacy and Safety of Flibanserin for the Treatment of Hypoactive Sexual Desire Disorder in Women: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis', JAMA Intern Med 2016;176:453-462

confidence_notes: Female sexual dysfunction is biopsychosocial and under-researched; psychological/relational/contextual factors dominate desire complaints. Vaginal estrogen helps genitourinary syndrome of menopause.

statement: Pelvic-floor muscle training (Kegels) has RCT/meta-analytic evidence for treating stress and mixed urinary incontinence in women and for speeding continence recovery after prostatectomy in men.
effect_size: Women doing PFMT ~8x more likely to report cure of stress incontinence vs controls (Cochrane)

provenance.primary: Dumoulin C et al., 'Pelvic floor muscle training versus no treatment for urinary incontinence in women', Cochrane Database Syst Rev 2018
provenance.surfaced_via: Wave-42 reproductive brief; cross-ref section 11 pelvic floor

confidence_notes: Genuinely effective and under-prescribed; technique matters (a physiotherapist improves results). Hypertonic pelvic floors need DOWN-training, not more Kegels. Cross-ref section 11 section 6.3.

statement: Despite lifelong sperm production, male fertility declines with paternal age: sperm DNA fragmentation rises, time-to-pregnancy lengthens, and offspring risk of certain conditions increases modestly.
effect_size: Advancing paternal age associated with longer time-to-pregnancy, higher miscarriage, increased de-novo mutations and modest rises in offspring autism/schizophrenia risk
population: Multiple large cohort and registry studies

provenance.primary: du Fosse NA et al., 'Advanced paternal age is associated with an increased risk of spontaneous miscarriage: a systematic review and meta-analysis', Hum Reprod Update 2020;26:650-669
provenance.surfaced_via: Wave-42 reproductive brief; male fertility decline

confidence_notes: Refutes the 'men have no fertility clock' myth; the decline is more gradual and later than the female one but real. The secular sperm-count decline (Levine) is contested and flagged as an open question, not a settled outcome.

statement: Premenstrual dysphoric disorder is a real, DSM-recognized severe form of PMS caused by abnormal sensitivity to normal hormone fluctuation (not abnormal hormone levels); SSRIs are effective and act rapidly.
effect_size: SSRIs (continuous or luteal-phase dosing) significantly reduce PMDD symptoms vs placebo (Cochrane)
population: Cochrane review of SSRIs for PMS/PMDD (31 RCTs)

provenance.primary: Marjoribanks J et al., 'Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors for premenstrual syndrome', Cochrane Database Syst Rev 2013

confidence_notes: PMDD is disabling and distinct from near-universal mild PMS. SSRIs work fast for PMDD (unlike in depression), supporting a distinct serotonergic mechanism. Cross-ref section 20 psychiatry.
